To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the toxicity of glutamate in cerebellar granular neurons is dependent on temperature, and that glutamate toxicity is dependent on non-NMDA glutamate receptors.
glutamate toxicity in cerebellar granular neurons is mediated by the activation of non-NMDARs and that the toxicity is potentiated when NMDARs are also activated.

1) glutamate is toxic to cerebellar granular neurons at 22 degrees C, 2) this toxicity is blocked by the NMDA receptor antagonist MK-801, 3) the toxicity is blocked by non-NMDA antagonists and 4) glutamate toxicity is potentiated by non-NMDAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of glutamate toxicity at reduced temperature.
the mechanisms by which glutamate induces neuronal damage in vitro.
the characterization of glutamate toxicity and the role of the NMDA and non-NMDA subtypes of glutamate receptors in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the toxicity of glutamate to cultured rat cerebellal granule neurons is mediated by the NMDA receptor, but that the non-NMDAR also contributes to the excitotoxicity of glutamate by promoting depolarization and the release of the NMDA Mg++ block.
the glutamate toxicity observed in these experiments was mediated by the activation of both the non-NMDARs and NMDARs.
glutamate toxicity at 22 degrees C is mediated by a synergistic interaction between non-NMDA and NMDA receptor activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the toxicity of glutamate to isolated neurons is mediated by both non-NMDA and NMDA receptor subtypes.
the non-NMDAR agonists are not toxic to granule cells at 22 degrees C in the absence of glutamate, but they can potentiate glutamate toxicity.
acute glutamate toxicity at reduced temperature is mediated by the activation of both NMDA and non-NMDA ionotropic receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the toxicity of glutamate in the CNS is dependent on temperature, and the temperature of the CNS is not constant.
the toxicity of glutamate to neurons is dependent on the temperature.
glutamate is not toxic in vitro at physiologic temperatures, but becomes so when the temperature is reduced, which suggests a mechanism that is not dependent on the presence of a toxic metabolite.
